text: Kingsmoor FC open the match with Viktor Quinlan scoring a penalty from the left side of the penalty area, approximately 9 metres from Westport Albion's goal. Minutes later, Quinlan scores again after a patient build-up featuring wide play and an 8-pass move. Westport Albion fight back, with Rafael Delacroix scoring twice close to the goal on the right flank after quick vertical passing sequences from regains. Early in the second half, Kenji Rahman nets a goal for Albion from a cross near the left edge of the penalty area to take the lead. Kingsmoor FC respond late despite a numerical disadvantage, with Luca Iversen scoring from close range on the left flank following a cross by Mason Morales. Tactical shifts saw Kingsmoor pressing higher and playing direct, while Westport dropped deeper and slowed play to protect their lead. Quinlan's all-round impact, with interceptions and key passes, earns him player of the match honors in this exciting and balanced contest [#152] [#222] [#401] [#553] [#983] [#1495] [#1516] [#1187] [#1459].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for audio audience in en

- Viktor Quinlan scored two early goals for Kingsmoor FC including a penalty at 8' with xg 0.76 and a second goal at 12' with xg 0.266, giving Kingsmoor a 2-0 lead [#152, #222].  
- Westport Albion responded with two goals from Rafael Delacroix at 22' (xg 0.768) and 30' (xg 0.973), leveling the score 2-2 by halftime [#401, #553].  
- Kenji Rahman scored for Westport Albion at 51' to give them a 3-2 lead with xg 0.693 [#983].  
- Kingsmoor FC’s Luca Iversen scored at 82' (xg 0.868) to equalize, despite Kingsmoor playing with 10 men after Felix Barros received a second yellow card at 81' [#1495, #1516].  
- Viktor Quinlan was named player of the match with 2 goals, 1.42 xg, 10 interceptions, 3 key passes, and a rating of 9.7 [player_of_the_match].

- Kingsmoor FC's goals reflect their wide crossing play typical of a 4-4-2 formation: the second goal at 12' was created through an 8-pass sequence started from a regain, involving wide players such as Felix Duarte, culminating in a close-range finish by Viktor Quinlan, showing an overload on wide areas and crossing attempts [220,222]. The late goal at 82' also came from a low-numbered passing sequence after recovery, finished off by Luca Iversen assisted by Mason Morales's cross, again emphasizing wide play and crossing from their 4-4-2 shape [1515,1516].
- Westport Albion operated a direct, vertical passing style in their own 4-4-2 formation, evident in their goals which often resulted from quick progression after regains, such as the 22' and 30' goals by Rafael Delacroix. These were assisted by short and crossing passes built through vertical, direct ball movement within about 7-10 passes and around 25-40 seconds duration from regains, exploiting quicker penetration and forward passes [399,401,552,553].
- The pattern of ball recovery seems tied to regains (transitions) for both sides before goals—Kingsmoor built patiently wide and crossing after regaining possession, while Westport pushed vertical and direct from regains, suggesting both teams capitalized on transitional moments aligned with their tactical identities [220,399,552].
- Tactical changes support this: Kingsmoor pressed higher and played more direct after 65' to chase the game, indicating a shift to more aggressive pressing and attack to regain lead, reflecting intent to increase ball recoveries high up and look for faster delivery forward [1187]. Westport Albion dropped deeper and slowed tempo after 79', to protect lead by reducing pressing intensity and conceding more possession, showing a defensive posture consistent with protecting advantage and limiting Kingsmoor's wide play impact [1459].
